skill.name: telegram-automation
skill.description: Guide Telegram bot operations through Rube MCP, including messages, media, chat details, updates, moderation actions, and command management.
skill.summary: Operate Telegram bots through current Rube MCP tool schemas and permission-aware workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 49 external-command alerts and 15 reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and Telegram parameter names. The documented Rube MCP endpoint creates an intentional third-party network dependency, so that low-severity finding is confirmed. No prompt injection, executable shell code, or covert data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The skill asks users to trust a third-party MCP endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Document the provider, data handling, and authentication flow, and advise users to verify the endpoint before connecting Telegram.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Telegram connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `telegram`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
2. `TELEGRAM_GET_CHAT` - Get chat details and verify access [Optional]
- `chat_id`: Numeric chat ID or channel username (e.g., '@channelname')
- `chat_id`: Chat where the message is located
- `message_id`: ID of the message to edit or delete
1. `TELEGRAM_FORWARD_MESSAGE` - Forward a message to another chat [Optional]
- `commands`: Array of command objects with `command` and `description`
- `callback_query_id`: ID of the callback query to answer
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Use offset to avoid processing the same update twice
1. Use '@username' format as chat_id (for public channels/groups)
2. For private chats, numeric chat_id is required
3. Use numeric chat_id in subsequent calls
| Forward message | TELEGRAM_FORWARD_MESSAGE | chat_id, from_chat_id, message_id |

content.value_statement: Telegram workflows often require several bot API calls and careful parameter handling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP operations.
actual_capabilities: Verifies the connected Telegram bot and retrieves chat details.
Sends text messages with plain text, HTML, or MarkdownV2 formatting.
Sends photos and documents with optional captions.
Edits, deletes, and forwards messages when bot permissions allow.
Retrieves updates, chat history, administrators, and member counts.
Sets bot commands and answers callback queries.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP, a connected Telegram bot, and suitable chat permissions.
Bots cannot initiate private conversations before a user starts them.
Telegram limits message length, caption length, file size, and request frequency.
History, moderation, and invite-link operations depend on chat type and administrator rights.

use_cases.title: Publish Community Updates
use_cases.description: Send formatted announcements, photos, and documents to groups or channels after verifying access.

use_cases.title: Handle Support Messages
use_cases.description: Review recent bot updates, reply to chats, and correct or remove bot messages.

use_cases.title: Maintain Bot Interactions
use_cases.description: Configure command menus, inspect callbacks, and manage message workflows with current tool schemas.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Text Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify my Telegram bot and target chat. Preview the message "[message]" for [chat], then wait for my approval before sending.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs to send one reviewed message.

prompt_templates.title: Share a Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Check access to [chat]. Prepare [document URL or file ID] with caption [caption], report any limits, and request approval before sending.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs to deliver a file safely.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Group
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve details, administrator names, and member count for [chat]. Do not export an invite link or change any Telegram state.
prompt_templates.scenario: A community manager needs a read-only group review.

prompt_templates.title: Process and Route Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch up to [limit] updates after offset [offset]. Summarize matching messages, propose destinations, and obtain approval before forwarding any message.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced workflow triages updates without duplicate processing.

output_examples.input: Prepare a maintenance notice for @project_updates and send it silently after approval.
output_examples.output: Bot identity and channel access verified. The final notice is ready for review, with silent delivery selected. No message has been sent yet.

output_examples.input: Show the administrators and member count for my support group.
output: No chat settings or messages changed.

output_examples.input: Update my bot command menu with help, status, and contact commands.
output_examples.output: The replacement command menu is prepared with three lowercase commands. Existing commands will be replaced only after approval.

best_practices: Search for current Rube tool schemas before every workflow.
Verify bot identity, target chat, permissions, and final content before external actions.
Track update offsets and respect Telegram rate and size limits.
anti_patterns: Do not send, delete, forward, or export invite links without explicit user approval.
Do not assume a username resolves to a private chat or that the bot has administrator rights.
Do not reuse stale schemas, ignore rate-limit responses, or process the same update twice.

faq.question: What connection does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Rube MCP and an active Telegram toolkit connection for your bot.

faq.question: Can it message any Telegram user?
faq.answer: No. Users must start private bot conversations, and the bot must have access to each target chat.

faq.question: Can it send files and photos?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports photo URLs, document URLs, existing file identifiers, and optional captions within Telegram limits.

faq.question: Can it edit or delete every message?
faq.answer: No. Editing is limited to bot messages, while deletion depends on age, ownership, and group permissions.

faq.question: Does it support formatted messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Telegram HTML and MarkdownV2 when reserved characters and supported tags are handled correctly.

faq.question: How does it prevent duplicate update processing?
faq.answer: Use the latest processed update offset when requesting the next batch of bot updates.
